reason: The hypothesis directly combines two well-established, separate mechanisms from the literature—crack-tip amorphization (P3) and grain boundary nanosegregation (P8, P23, P34)—into a single competitive framework controlled by deformation conditions (temperature and strain rate). This specific integration, proposing a direct trade-off between these two mechanisms to govern toughness retention, is not stated in any single passage and represents a synthesis of findings from distinct papers.
copied_elements: deformation-induced crystalline-to-amorphous phase transformation and amorphous nanobridges at crack tips (P3)
fast nanosegregation of principal elements (Ni, Cr) at grain boundaries reducing cohesion and causing intergranular cracking (P8, P23, P34)
ductility loss at intermediate temperatures due to grain boundary segregation (P8, P23, P34)
